extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent attorneys and agents preparing and filing PCT (international) patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing, filing and prosecuting an international application under the PCT (contents, form, language, deadlines, receiving Offices, national phase entry, and associated procedural rules). Intended to direct applicants and their agents on compliance with PCT formalities and strategic use of PCT procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation when filed in non-accepted language
rubrics_metrics.description: If an international application is filed in a language which is not both a language accepted by the International Searching Authority which is to carry out the international search and a language of publication, it needs to be translated into an appropriate language shortly after filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations required by Offices of or acting for countries where protection is sought are generally prepared much later; only the translations needed for international search/publication must be furnished shortly after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for national/regional fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees payable to national or regional Patent Offices become due later than without the PCT and are payable only if the applicant proceeds with national/regional processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such national or regional fees generally must be paid within the same time limit as referred to in paragraph 4.016 (see national phase entry time limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for entering national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicable time limit for entering the national phase is 30 months from the priority date (or later in some cases) for all Offices except those where an earlier time limit remains applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some Offices remain at former 20-month (or 21-month) limits unless applicant files a demand for international preliminary examination before 19 months; consult Official Notices (PCT Gazette), PCT Newsletter, National Chapters, and WIPO time limits table for up-to-date exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of a favorable international search report (ISR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A favorable international search report (and any supplementary ISR) strengthens the applicant's position vis-à-vis national/regional Patent Offices and makes arguments for grant more convincing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use favorable ISRs strategically to support national phase prosecution; unfavorable reports may prompt claim amendment or abandonment to save costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of international preliminary report on patentability (IPRP)
rubrics_metrics.description: A favorable international preliminary report on patentability under Chapter I or II contains far more material on chances of obtaining patents than an ISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider requesting international preliminary examination to obtain a more substantive opinion on patentability before national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to partly favorable/unfavorable ISR or written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: If ISR and written opinion are partly favorable and partly unfavorable, the applicant can modify the claims to keep only those likely to result in grant; if unfavorable, applicant may decide not to proceed to save costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same considerations apply to supplementary ISRs and to IPRPs under Chapter II.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT procedural advantages (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT route provides savings in the procedure before designated Offices (e.g., no need to provide original drawings or certified priority copies to each Office) and reduction in national fees in several countries and the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consider these procedural and cost-saving advantages when deciding to use PCT and when selecting designated/elected Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined use with regional patent systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The PCT is fully compatible with regional patent systems (ARIPO Harare Protocol, Eurasian Patent Convention, European Patent Convention, OAPI Agreement), enabling combined filing routes (ARIPO‑PCT, Eurasian‑PCT, Euro‑PCT, OAPI‑PCT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a PCT application can have simultaneous filing effect with regional Offices; applicants can wait for PCT search/examination results and use extended periods for translations and appointment of agents before proceeding with regional procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to obtain both regional and national protection via PCT
rubrics_metrics.description: A national of a State party to a regional treaty may file a PCT application and designate all PCT Contracting States to obtain, where applicable, both regional and national patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits reverse-direction combined use of PCT with regional routes instead of filing separate regional and national applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euro-PCT validation/extension possibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Euro-PCT route may allow extension or validation of European patents into some States not party to the European Patent Convention if the international application designates both the national patent of the State and a European patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Annex B (EP) and National Chapter (EP) for details and conditions; relevant once a European patent is granted based on the PCT application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of international application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is 'international' when filed under and with reference to the PCT; it is the first step towards obtaining a patent in or for a State party to the PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International application may be used to pursue national patents or regional patents (ARIPO, Eurasian, European, OAPI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible subject matter for an international application
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application must be an application for the protection of an invention; PCT encompasses patents, inventors’ certificates, utility certificates, utility models, and certificates of addition; purely ornamental designs fall outside scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not file PCT applications for subject matter that is not an 'invention' under PCT Articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main legal effects of an international application
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application has two main effects: it has an international filing date and is produced in/for the designated States where applicant wishes to obtain a patent; it also has prior art effect as applicable under national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check National Chapters (e.g., US) for specific prior art effect details; international filing date is accorded as of international filing date (see paragraph 6.005).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elected States definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated States for which international preliminary examination has been demanded by the applicant are called elected States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election matters for Chapter II international preliminary examination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delaying effect on national processing and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, no designated Office may process or examine the international application prior to the expiration of 30 months from the priority date; fees and translations to designated Offices will usually be due by that 30‑month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some designated Offices continue to apply former 20- or 21-month limits or have later limits; consult National Chapters and Official Notices for variations. This delaying effect postpones national/regional examination and grant procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of demanding international preliminary examination on deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: If international preliminary examination is demanded before 19 months, the delaying effect will be 10 months longer in respect of any State whose designated Office has notified incompatibility with the modified Article 22(1), making the deadline effectively 30 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed information about specific Offices and later time limits is available in National Phase and National Chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of international filing date for priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application accorded an international filing date is equivalent to a regular national filing under the Paris Convention and may be invoked as basis of priority claim in subsequent national, regional or international applications within Convention time limits and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of PCT filing for claiming priority follows Paris Convention rules (Article 8, Article 11(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to file (receiving Offices and International Bureau)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annexes B indicate which authorities (receiving Offices) nationals/residents may use to file international applications; alternatively the International Bureau may act as receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple applicants are nationals/residents of different States any receiving Office of a Contracting State of which at least one applicant is a resident/national is competent. Residents/nationals of States party to certain regional systems may also file with regional Offices. Applicants must comply with national security prescriptions; receiving Offices may apply measures accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice between different receiving Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may have a choice between several receiving Offices where applicable (e.g., multiple applicants of different nationalities or a sole applicant with multiple nationalities/residences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of RO can affect language, fees, and procedural details; check Annex C for receiving Office requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements of an international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Any international application must contain: request, description, claim(s), one or more drawings (where necessary for understanding), and abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed information on each element is provided in following paragraphs; missing elements may lead to irregularities or loss of filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of elements in application
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements must be arranged in the following order: request, description, claim(s), abstract, drawing(s) (if any). Any sequence listing part of the description must be provided as a separate electronic file (XML).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict ordering is required; sequence listings have specific filing format requirements (XML).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheet numbering requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All sheets must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals with three series of numbers: first for the request, second for description+claims+abstract, third for drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 11.7(a) and Section 207(b) numbering to ensure correct processing and referencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language(s) of filing and translation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Language in which an international application must be filed depends on the receiving Office. If filed in a language other than those accepted for publication (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish) or not accepted by the ISA, a translation will need to be furnished for international search/publication and possibly supplementary search or international preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All elements must normally be in the same language except language-dependent free text in a sequence listing if permitted. The request must be in a language of publication accepted by the receiving Office; text in drawings and abstract may be in publication language. Most cases require only one translation for the international phase; see Annexes and paragraphs 6.013–6.020, 8.012, 9.017–9.019, 10.011 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure if not filed in language accepted by receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an international application is not filed in a language accepted by the receiving Office, special procedures apply (refer to paragraph 6.034).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the specified paragraph for detailed steps; non-accepted language filings may require timely furnishing of a translation or may affect filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of the Request (PCT/RO/101) and electronic filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where filed electronically the Request Form is generated by the electronic filing system. For paper filings, the request must be on printed Form PCT/RO/101 or a compliant computer print-out, or the editable PDF version downloadable from WIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completed forms are available from receiving Offices and the International Bureau; follow Administrative Instructions for paper submissions and electronic systems for e-filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory indications in the Request
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must contain the title of the invention; identify the applicant, normally the inventor, and the agent (if any); the filing constitutes designation of all Contracting States; the request should also contain, where applicable, a priority claim, choice of competent ISA, and reference to any relevant earlier search; the request must be signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed box-by-box instructions for filling the request form are provided later; ensure language of request complies with language rules (5.013).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant file reference (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended that the applicant indicate his/her file reference (if any), not exceeding 25 characters, in the box provided on the request form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File reference may be letters and/or numerals with hyphen as separator; receiving Office, IB, ISA and IPEA will use it in correspondence; see paragraphs 5.105, 10.015 and 11.071 for marking file references on other documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical requirements for request text
rubrics_metrics.description: Any text matter in the request must be in characters the capital letters of which are not less than 0.21 cm high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 11.9(d) to avoid illegibility objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of invention requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title must be short (preferably two to seven words, when in English or translated into English) and precise. The same title must be given in Box No. I of the request and at the beginning of the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly long or vague titles; follow Rule 4.3 and Rule 5.1(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file (entitlement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any resident or national of a Contracting State may file an international application. Where there are two or more applicants, at least one must be a national or resident of a Contracting State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competence of receiving Office depends on residence/nationality; see PCT Contracting States listing and paragraph 5.023 on residence/nationality determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different applicants for different designated States
rubrics_metrics.description: Different applicants may be indicated for various designated States, but different applicants may not be indicated for different types of protection in a State; for national and regional designation of a State, the same applicant(s) must be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Article 9(3) and Section 203(b) rules; check Annex B for country-specific requirements on types of protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of residence and nationality
rubrics_metrics.description: Residence and nationality are determined by the national law of the State and decided by the receiving Office. Possession of a real and effective industrial or commercial establishment counts as residence; a legal entity constituted under national law is a national.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing with the International Bureau as RO and a question arises, the IB will request the national Office to decide and inform the applicant; the applicant may submit arguments directly to that national Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: How the applicant must be identified in the Request
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must be identified by name and address and by marking check-boxes indicating whether the person is also inventor or applicant only; where applicant is a corporation, mark 'applicant only'. Registration numbers may be added; nationality and residence must be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 4.5; later changes to person/name/address are handled under paragraphs 11.018–11.022.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Names of natural persons must be indicated by family name followed by given name(s); academic degrees/titles must be omitted; family name preferably in capital letters. Legal entity names by full official designation preferably in caps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 4.4(a–b) to ensure consistent identification across Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses must be indicated so as to satisfy prompt postal delivery and must include all relevant administrative units up to house number (if any) and the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 4.4(c); include telephone/fax/e-mail if no agent is indicated and consider providing email for rapid notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision and use of contact details and email notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended to provide telephone, facsimile and e-mail if no agent is indicated; if an e-mail address is provided, the receiving Office, ISA and IB may send notifications by e-mail and usually will not send paper notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is responsible to keep e-mail up-to-date and ensure messages are not blocked; changes should be requested to be recorded (preferably at IB) under Rule 92bis. Check Annex B to see which Authorities provide email notification services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special correspondence address and one address per applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one address may be indicated for each applicant in Box No. II or III; where no agent is indicated, a special address for correspondence may be given in Box IV; a common representative may indicate a correspondence address in Box IV different from the applicant's address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 4.4(d) to ensure correct routing of notices and correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why nationality and residence must be indicated
rubrics_metrics.description: Nationality and residence are needed to determine entitlement to file internationally and competence of the receiving Office; indicate names of country of which applicant is national and resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If country of residence is not specified but appears in address it will be assumed; procedures exist for 'non-competent' receiving Office filings (see para 6.035).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of applicant indications when multiple applicants exist
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one applicant exists, it is advisable to provide indications (name/address/nationality/residence) for all; however if at least one entitled applicant has provided the required indications, the receiving Office will not invite missing indications for others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 26.2bis(b); still advisable to include full details to avoid later complications.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to indicate names of States
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of any State may be indicated by full name, short title or two-letter code as set out in WIPO Standard ST.3 (Country Names and Two-Letter Codes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the accepted short names/two-letter codes listed in WIPO Standard ST.3 (formerly Annex K) to ensure consistency across PCT documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which applicant should be named first
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended that the applicant who will represent all applicants and to whom notifications are to be sent be named first; that applicant will be considered the common representative if no common agent/representative is appointed and if entitled to file with the receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a common agent or representative is indicated in Box IV, notices will be sent to that agent or representative instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of inventor in the request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the person in Box II is also the inventor, mark 'This person is also inventor' and no repetition in Box III is required. If inventor is identified in Box III, mark 'applicant and inventor' if inventor is also applicant or 'inventor only' if not. Special provisions exist when inventors differ per designated State or are deceased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Article 4(1)(v), Rule 4.1(a)(iv) and Rule 4.6; include inventor data unless national law of none of the designated States requires it at national filing, though inclusion is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to mark 'inventor only' checkbox
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the inventor is not also an applicant, check 'inventor only' and indicate name and address in a sub-box of Box III. The name/address may be omitted where national law of none of the designated States requires inventor name at time of filing, but inclusion is recommended unless special reasons prevent it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Article 4(4) and Rule 4.1(c)(i) and check Annexes B for country-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for inventor name/address and country indication
rubrics_metrics.description: The indication rules for inventor name/address follow those for applicant; country of inventor need not be provided unless inventor is also applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For later changes in inventor identification, see paragraphs 11.018 and 11.020.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitting different inventors for different designated States
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT permits different inventors to be indicated for different designated States where national laws differ; indicate for which States a named person is inventor in the Supplemental Box (item 1(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all inventors are the same for all designated States, no special indication is required; follow Rule 4.6(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of designated States for several applicants (request box checkboxes)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the bottom of Box II and each sub-box of Box III there are two check-boxes; one (but only one) must be marked for an applicant who is an applicant for all designated States or for specific States indicated in the Supplemental Box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed explanation of these check-boxes and how to indicate designated States is given in paragraphs 5.052 to 5.054 and in the filled-in sample of the request form.
